question: Will Gavin Newsom call a special session of the California Legislature on AI before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: topics Newsom has publicly floated for a special session; few become proclamations (wildfire liability floated repeatedly in 2026, not called). Key update up: on Sept 17 he explicitly floated an AI special session, and Executive Order N-9-26 sets a Nov 16 recommendations deadline described as a possible basis for one. The new Legislature's convening in early Dec is a natural vehicle, as in Nov 2024, and only the proclamation counts. Down: he offered executive/agency action as alternatives, says lawmakers must be willing participants, has weak lame-duck leverage (the wildfire deal collapsed, Rivas' 'half measures' criticism), and leaves office in Jan. No human prediction market found for this contract; the Manifold market on completing his term (0.97) is only tangential.
calls.dossier:
- Sept 17 2026 (POLITICO, via CalMatters/KQED): Newsom said he intends further AI safety action before leaving office in Jan 2027, via a special session, executive action, or agency steps under existing authority.
- Sept 18 2026: Executive Order N-9-26 directs GovOps and Cal OES to recommend AI framework amendments by Nov 16 2026 (kill switch, onsite verifiers, broader incident definition). CalMatters: the recommendations 'could form the basis of a special legislative session.' CASRAI: the EO orders recommendations only and mandates no kill switch.
- Early Oct 2026 (Carrier Management/AP, Oct 2): Newsom signed AI worker-protection and chatbot risk-assessment laws; he 'left the door open' to calling lawmakers back for a special session on AI.
- Sen. Scott Wiener (CalMatters, Sept 2026) praised the EO and urged haste. No statements found from Speaker Rivas or Pro Tem Limón on an AI special session.
- CalMatters, Sept 2 2026: Newsom's lame-duck leverage is weak. The wildfire-liability deal collapsed at session end; Rivas criticized 'half measures'; Newsom said a special session would need lawmakers as willing participants ('I'm just not going to leave without trying').
- Yahoo/AP, Sept 2026: on wildfire liability, Newsom repeatedly declined to rule out a special session but implied a deal was more likely under the next governor. This topic was floated but has not become a proclamation to date.
- Precedent: Newsom proclaimed special sessions in 2024 (gas prices) and on Nov 7 2024 (litigation funding vs. the Trump administration), the latter timed for the new Legislature's Dec 2 swearing-in with leaders' pre-agreement.
- Calendar: the 2025-26 Legislature's term ends Nov 30 2026; the new Legislature convenes the first Monday of Dec 2026 (Dec 7). Newsom leaves office in early Jan 2027.
- Status quo: no proclamation on AI has been issued as of Oct 5 2026 (none found in searches).
- Resolves off a proclamation published at gov.ca.gov, leginfo, or the Assembly/Senate Daily Journals, not off whether a session convenes or passes anything. Amending another special-session proclamation to add AI also counts.
- Event window: Oct 1 2026 -> Dec 31 2026 per the criteria; as of Oct 5 2026 about 5% has elapsed.
- Markets: no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found on this question. The only related Manifold market is on Newsom completing his term.
- Searched but not found: legislative leaders' responses to an AI special session; any October 2026 reporting of firm special-session plans; the full POLITICO article (fetch blocked).

Against: he explicitly lists executive/agency action as alternatives, very little lame-duck time remains to pass and sign bills before he leaves office in early Jan 2027, industry opposition, no reported legislative-leader buy-in, and the new Legislature could pursue it in regular session under the next governor. calls.reasoning: Status quo is No: as of Oct 5, 2026 there is no proclamation. Topics Newsom floats for special sessions often never become proclamations; wildfire liability in 2026 is the example. Up: he floated an AI special session on Sept 17 and said again in early October that he is 'contemplating' one for a kill switch. EO N-9-26's Nov 16 recommendations line up with the new Legislature convening Dec 7, which mirrors his Nov 2024 proclamation, and only the proclamation counts. Down: he is a lame duck with weak leverage after the wildfire deal collapsed. He himself called special sessions a 'four-letter word' among some legislators and said they carry 'peril'. Legislative leaders have not endorsed one, executive and agency routes already exist, and the industry opposes a kill switch. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts and differ by judgment (0.22-0.33). Check 1: the SF Chronicle and Fox5 confirm that at an early-October news conference Newsom said he is 'contemplating calling a special legislative session' for a kill switch. That shows the idea survived the EO and slightly supports the higher runs. Check 2: no statement found from Speaker Rivas or the Senate Pro Tem. Politico via Yahoo shows Newsom acknowledging that some legislators see special sessions as a 'four-letter word' and that they carry 'peril', which weighs against, together with his lame-duck status and the uncalled wildfire session. The rest is judgment. A proclamation is cheap and the December convening is a plausible vehicle, but the session would mostly run under his successor and executive routes already exist. I bet 0.25.
